key_insight: GRC frames continual learning as recursive residual closure, showing when an agent should update internal parameters versus revise its representation to stay both stable and plastic.
engineering_relevance: This provides a principled update rule for systems that must retain prior responsibilities while safely adapting to new conditions, relevant to adaptive control, optimization, and learning-based constitutive modeling.
method: Defines learning as closing future-relevant residuals under a fixed learner-world boundary.
Derives a local tangent decomposition that separates in-representation transformation from representation revision.
Proves an affine constrained quadratic update with a stability-plasticity compatibility condition and a unique safe-response solution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytic results and proof-based criteria, including a necessary-and-sufficient condition, uniqueness of the update solution, and theoretical comparisons of safe-response operators, rather than empirical dataset evaluation.
watch_item: The framework relies on regularity assumptions and a fixed representation-relation boundary, so practical deployment may require careful model design and verification of the stated conditions.
paper_title: Generalized Residual Closure: General Learning Dynamics for Stability-Plasticity Compatibility
